chase_cards.name: Imakuni?
chase_cards.why: This row is not valuable because it is elegant; it is valuable because it shows the TCG's human theater. Imakuni? is the mascot-performer, the joke, the confusion mechanic, and possibly the person handing the card across the table.

key_artists.name: Takumi Akabane
key_artists.why: Bulbapedia's gallery labels the unnumbered promotional print as Photo. Takumi Akabane; this matters because Imakuni? is a photo-card and one of the early moments where a real person enters the card frame.

claims.text: The local catalog models the Tropical Mega Battle Hawaii Games participation prize as a one-row unnumbered promotional source group containing Imakuni? at source index 130.
Bulbapedia's unnumbered promotional list identifies source row 130 as Imakuni? [Non-Glossy], Trainer, distributed as a Tropical Mega Battle Hawaii Games participation prize on August 25, 1999.
Bulbapedia says a regular card-stock version of Imakuni? was given away during the first Tropical Mega Battle at Hilton Hawaiian Village in Honolulu between August 24 and 27, 1999.
Bulbapedia's gallery labels the unnumbered promotional Imakuni? print with a Photo. Takumi Akabane credit.
Bulbapedia notes that this was the first Pokemon card to use Photo. instead of Illus. in the normal credit position and one of only a few cards with a real-life person image.
Bulbapedia says it is possible Tomoaki Imakuni himself gave away these regular card-stock copies while casually playing people in costume with his Confusion Deck at the event.

The row matters because it turns a performer from Pokemon Card Game commercials into a physical event object: the card is both a joke Trainer and a trace of the human show around the first Tropical Mega Battle.

Agents should preserve row 130, Imakuni? name, Tropical Mega Battle Hawaii Games participation-prize route, regular card-stock / non-glossy signal, Takumi Akabane photo credit, and non-equivalence with glossy CoroCoro and later Supporter reprints before accepting a match.

narrative.human_title: Imakuni? at Hawaii: the card game turns around and waves
narrative.why_it_matters: This is one of the great little assembly objects. The Tropical Mega Battle was already Pokemon becoming international tournament culture, and then here is Imakuni?: a real performer, a TV-commercial singer, a confusion joke, a photo credit, and maybe the person actually handing the thing to players in Hawaii. The card is silly on purpose, but the silliness is historical evidence. It shows that Pokemon was built by shows, songs, people in costumes, kids at tables, and cardboard that knew it was part of the act.

narrative.human_title: Imakuni? 130: a real person in the cardboard machine
narrative.why_it_matters: This card is the grin in the archive. It is a Trainer card, but also a photo card, an event handout, a song-and-commercial memory, and a little rules joke that makes confusion literal. An agent should not treat Imakuni? as just a name to match. It has to know which Imakuni? this is: the regular-stock Hawaii Games print from the first Tropical Mega Battle route.
